@@ -0,0 +1,175 @@
+// interface stubs for the Delphi LLVM 32-bit ARM compiler (Android armeabi-v7a)
+//   armfakestub   = TInterfacedObjectFake methods (SOA client side)
+//   armcallmethod = CallMethod() for RawExecute (SOA server side, callbacks)
+//   armfakethunks = the VMT entry points, one per method index
+// counterpart of delphi-aarch64.s, used by mormot.core.interfaces.pas when
+// DELPHI_ARM32_STUBS is defined
+//
+// build with the clang of the NDK shipped with the RAD Studio Android SDK
+// (see compile.sh)
+//
+// Delphi follows AAPCS with VFP hard-float: R0..R3 and D0..D7 carry the
+// parameters, but a by-ref result (string, dynarray, record...) is passed in
+// R0 and Self in R1 - the opposite of FPC, see DELPHI_RESULT_FIRST
+//
+// armfakestub is entered from one of the thunks below, with
+//   R12 = method index, R0..R3 / D0..D7 / stack = parameters
+// it builds a TFakeCallStack (ABIA32 layout) at SP+4, i.e. 132 bytes below
+// the caller stack arguments:
+//   +0   ParamRegs   R0..R3
+//   +16  FPRegs      D0..D7
+//   +80  MethodIndex (R12)
+//   +84  Frame, +88 Ret, +92 DummyStack[0..9] (R11/LR saved at +124/+128)
+//   +132 Stack       = caller stack arguments
+// then calls fakecall(Instance = R0, Stack), i.e. the exported
+// TInterfacedObjectFakeRaw.FakeCall redirection, which returns the ordinal
+// result in R0:R1 and stores any float result into FPRegs[D0]
+//
+// NOTE: the .fnstart/.save/.setfp directives are mandatory: Delphi uses the
+// ARM EHABI unwinder, so an exception raised within FakeCall must be able to
+// unwind through this frame
+// - everything is ARM (not Thumb) code: the VMT entries are then plain even
+// addresses, and the linker adds the interworking to/from the Delphi code
+
+    .syntax unified
+    .arm
+    .fpu vfpv3-d16
+
+    .text
+    .p2align 2
+    .global armfakestub
+    .type armfakestub, %function
+
+armfakestub:
+    .fnstart
+    push {r11, lr}
+    .save {r11, lr}
+    mov r11, sp
+    .setfp r11, sp
+    sub sp, sp, #128                // SP = entry - 136, still 8-byte aligned
+
+    str r12, [sp, #84]              // MethodIndex at +80
+    add r12, sp, #4                 // R12 = TFakeCallStack
+    stm r12, {r0-r3}
+    add r1, r12, #16
+    vstm r1, {d0-d7}
+
+    mov r1, r12                     // R0 = Instance, R1 = Stack
+    bl  fakecall
+
+    // FakeCall stored any float result into FPRegs[D0]
+    vldr d0, [sp, #20]
+
+    mov sp, r11
+    pop {r11, pc}
+    .fnend
+    .size armfakestub, .-armfakestub
+
+
+// the VMT entry points, one per method index - compiled in instead of JITted,
+// as for aarch64 (and Android may forbid rwx pages in the future)
+// - the count has to match MAX_METHOD_COUNT of mormot.core.interfaces (a
+//   {$message fatal} there guards the other direction)
+// - entry i is armfakethunks + i * 8: method index into R12, then on to
+//   armfakestub (b reaches +-32 MB, and both live in the same section)
+//
+// armfakethunkbase returns the address of that table, as a function - Delphi
+// wraps an "external ... name" procedure in a thunk of its own, so taking
+// @armfakethunks in Pascal yields the wrapper, not the table
+// - it sits right before the table: ADR only encodes small offsets in ARM mode
+
+    .p2align 2
+    .global armfakethunkbase
+    .type armfakethunkbase, %function
+
+armfakethunkbase:
+    .fnstart
+    adr r0, .Lfakethunks            // PC + 8 = the table itself
+    bx  lr
+    .fnend
+    .size armfakethunkbase, .-armfakethunkbase
+
+    .global armfakethunks
+    .type armfakethunks, %function
+
+armfakethunks:
+.Lfakethunks:
+    .fnstart
+    .cantunwind                     // reached by b, never a return address
+    .set fakethunkindex, 0
+    .rept 128
+    mov r12, #fakethunkindex
+    b   armfakestub
+    .set fakethunkindex, fakethunkindex + 1
+    .endr
+    .fnend
+    .size armfakethunk

commits.subject: all: make the Delphi Android 32-bit (ARMv7) target work
commits.body:
- interfaces: external stubs for the Delphi LLVM ARM compiler
  (res/static/delphillvm/delphi-arm.s -> delphi-android-arm.o): armfakestub,
  armcallmethod and 128 compiled-in VMT thunks, as done for aarch64
- the Delphi ARM ABI is VFP hard-float (as CPUARMHF), but passes a by-ref
  result in R0 and Self in R1, just like Delphi on Linux x64: so
  DELPHI_SYSVX64_RESULT_FIRST becomes DELPHI_RESULT_FIRST, using
  PARAMREG_FIRST/PARAMREG_RESULT (same values as REGRDI/REGRSI on SysV x64),
  and DELPHI_AARCH64_STATIC_FAKEVMT becomes DELPHI_STATIC_FAKEVMT
- json: ARMv7 raises an alignment fault on VLDR/LDRD at an address which is
  not 4-byte aligned, and unaligned() is a no-op on Delphi: float and Int64
  fields of packed records go through an aligned copy (DELPHI_ARM32_UNALIGNED)
- variants: DispInvoke reads the ARM va_list, i.e. @VAList with 8-byte
  aligned 64-bit values (DISPINVOKE_AAPCS32)
- defines: EXTENDEDTOSHORT_USESTR + DOUBLETOSHORT_USEGRISU (FloatToText gives
  15 digits only), and CPU_ARCH_TEXT uses ABIA32 since NOASMBLOCK undefines
  CPUARM

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HnjnbKNBTbM2GpoD2YuHCC

commits.subject: net: TDelphiNetHttp as a single class, no new unit
commits.body:
As requested in the review: the separate mormot.lib.nethttp wrapper is gone,
TDelphiNetHttp holds the THTTPClient and the whole logic itself.

- the RTL units are listed first in the interface uses clause, so that the
  mORMot identifiers declared afterwards (e.g. TUri) take precedence
- the request is created in InternalCreateRequest, headers are added line by
  line as TCurlHttp does, body and answer go through TRawByteStringStream
- the certificate callback is a method of the class
- mormot.defines.inc keeps its {$ifdef OSANDROID} ... {$else} layout: Delphi
  iOS gets USEDELPHINETHTTP and NOGSSAPIAUTH in its own {$ifdef IOS} block

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HnjnbKNBTbM2GpoD2YuHCC
commits.author: Stefan Diestelmann

commits.subject: core: name the library for the mach externals on Darwin
commits.body:
A bare "external 'mach_task_self'" makes the Delphi Darwin linker look for a
file named like the symbol, and the link fails with
"ld: file not found: mach_task_self". Use clib for all four declarations,
exactly as the neighbouring mach_absolute_time/mach_timebase_info already do -
one version for both compilers.
